layers.name: artifact_invariant_compatibility_signals
layers.description: Signals that recur across artifact classes regardless of representation form

signals.mechanism: Operates on evidence metadata (behavioral evaluation presence/absence, QA status), not on structural measurements. Representation-agnostic by design.

Composite of QA gating + task-relation boundaries + structural risk. The narrowing logic (broad input -> narrow output) is preserved even when the structural risk computation differs by representation.
The ordering same_task > same_family > cross_task is upstream of representation form. It reflects task similarity, not factor geometry. Present in all classes where testable.
Same-family pairs occupy a distinct middle ground. This follows from task-relation ordering. Confirmed in LoRA and checkpoint delta but not testable in LoHa.

layers.name: representation_family_features
layers.description: Signals that are meaningful only within one representation family

signals.description: Factor-level subspace geometry including the V-module dimensionality ratio
Strategy selection for factor-based merge execution
Stable rank, utilization, energy rank from SVD of factor matrices
Pairwise comparison via cosine similarity of per-layer summary vectors
Effective rank, stable rank, energy concentrations from full delta matrix SVD
Truncated SVD reconstruction error from materialized conversion

layers.name: decision_dependent_interpretation
layers.description: How compatibility signals are interpreted depends on the decision scenario

scenarios.interpretation: Worst-case aggregation. Factor geometry matters. Strategy recommendation is actionable. Only available for LoRA (native) and LoHa (shimmed, unvalidated).
Distributional aggregation. Confusability scoring. Task-family routing. Available for LoRA (routing pilot). Not tested for other classes.
QA-gate-first aggregation. Evidence status dominates. Available for all three classes. This is the only decision scenario with full cross-artifact coverage.

interaction_rules: Layer 1 signals (invariant) can be referenced across artifact classes without qualification.
Layer 2 signals (representation-local) must be qualified by artifact class when referenced.
Layer 3 scenarios determine which Layer 2 signals are relevant in a given decision context.
Only triage (Layer 3) has complete cross-artifact coverage. Merge and routing are artifact-local in practice.
Numeric compatibility scores from Layer 2 cannot be compared across representation families.
